name: Talk2Me Buttons
author: Randy Adams

sections.description:
Talk2Me Buttons adds a floating “Talk2Me” button to your website. When a visitor clicks it, they start a real voice conversation with an AI agent that can sound like you and knows your business.

This plugin doesn’t just paste a code snippet — it includes a guided setup wizard that walks you through the whole process of creating your widget:

  1. Get started in your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Create your widget on Talk2Me (opens in a new tab): sign up, record a short voice sample to clone your voice, add your photo, and point the agent at your website so it learns what you sell.
  3. Connect it back in WordPress by pasting your widget ID (or the full embed snippet).
  4. Go live — the button is installed on your site automatically. No theme editing, no copy-pasting scripts into your header.

You can turn the button on or off any time from the Settings screen, and update the connected widget whenever you like. The Settings screen also links you straight to your Talk2Me dashboard to change your agent’s greeting, update its knowledge base, swap its photo and voice, and view conversation analytics.

Features

  • Guided, step-by-step setup wizard that launches on activation.
  • One-click connect: paste your widget ID or the whole embed snippet — the ID is detected for you.
  • Site-wide floating button, loaded efficiently in the footer.
  • [talk2me_button] shortcode to force-load the button on a specific page.
  • Quick links from Settings to manage your agent’s greeting, knowledge, photo, voice, and analytics on your Talk2Me dashboard.
  • Clean uninstall — removes its options when deleted.

Account required

Creating a Talk2Me widget requires a Talk2Me account and, to publish the button to your live site, a Talk2Me subscription. The plugin guides you to talk2mebuttons.com to set this up. See the External Services section below.

External services

This plugin connects to two external services operated by Talk2Me:

1. Talk2Me app (talk2mebuttons.com)
The setup wizard links you to https://talk2mebuttons.com to create your widget (sign up, clone your voice, add a photo, build your agent, and subscribe). This happens in a new browser tab on the Talk2Me site; the plugin itself does not transmit your data there. Your use of that site is governed by Talk2Me’s Terms of Service (https://talk2me.ai/terms-of-service) and Privacy Policy (https://talk2me.ai/privacy-policy).

2. Talk2Me embed script (popup.talk2me.bot)
When the button is enabled, your site loads a small JavaScript file from https://popup.talk2me.bot/embed.js on your front-end pages. This script renders the floating button and powers the voice conversation. It is loaded with your widget ID (the “slug” you connect during setup). This request is made from your visitors’ browsers when they view your site. Data handled by conversations with the widget is processed by Talk2Me under the policies linked above.

No data is sent to these services from your WordPress admin beyond what you choose to do on the Talk2Me site.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the talk2me-buttons folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin through the WordPress Plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen in WordPress.
  3. You’ll be taken to the Talk2Me setup wizard automatically. Follow the steps to create and connect your widget.
  4. Your talking button is now live in the bottom-right corner of your site.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Talk2Me account?

Yes. The plugin installs and controls the button on your WordPress site, but the widget itself (your voice, your agent, your subscription) is created and hosted on Talk2Me. The setup wizard walks you through it.

I already have a widget. Can I skip the wizard?

Yes. Go to Talk2Me → Settings, paste your widget ID (or embed snippet), enable the button, and save.

Where does the button appear?

By default it floats in the bottom-right corner of every page. If you prefer to load it only on specific pages, turn off the site-wide setting and add the [talk2me_button] shortcode to those pages.

How do I remove the button?

Turn off “Show button on site” in Settings, or deactivate the plugin.
